records.region: Áncash, western Cordillera Negra and Casma coastal valley
records.candidate_name_role: Supported representative receiving-system identity, without assigning that name to every upper reach or tributary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The continuously researched westward highland-to-Pacific selection belongs to the Casma receiving system. The study distinguishes Chacchan and Grande along its upper and middle main course; their names are retained as bounded reach observations. The chosen uppermost small drainage is not given a precise reach-name boundary.
records.completion_scope: Río Casma is supported as the representative receiving-system identity. All 23 selected parts were followed from the chosen eastern highland drainage through connected mountain valleys, the broad cultivated lower corridor and coastal receiving floor to the Pacific. The original 2007 local basin study supplies the naming sequence; three independently maintained satellite-mosaic views supply the geographic correspondence. Upper reach names and the two stored terminal positions remain separately described.
records.supported_name_scope: The continuously researched westward highland-to-Pacific selection belongs to the Casma receiving system. The study distinguishes Chacchan and Grande along its upper and middle main course; their names are retained as bounded reach observations. The chosen uppermost small drainage is not given a precise reach-name boundary.

scope_limits: The selected initial small drainage is geographically connected to the receiving system, but its precise local hydronym and the boundaries between report-described upper names are not resolved. This does not prevent a Casma representative-system identity.
The report’s Huarancayoc, Ruri Ruri, Chacchan and Grande sequence is not treated as a set of true aliases for the whole selection. Pira, Vado, Yaután and Sechín remain separate contributing rivers.

The generalized final route crosses cultivated coastal receiving ground and ends just offshore near the lower drainage outlets. It is not asserted to trace the presently active mouth or every bank exactly.

Mosaic acquisition dates, seasonal water conditions, irrigation operation, current flow, bank alignment and tidal edge are unverified. Ordinary connected valley and coastal-floor geography is sufficient for this finding.
Formal registry status and a Korean name remain unverified; no automatic or product name application is authorized or performed.

records.region: Québec, eastern James Bay; Pontax receiving corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: The named northern river and its common lower receiving corridor, researched together with the selected southern Machisakahikanistikw branch. Does not rename every selected branch or wetland passage.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded ordinary geographic correspondence for both selected roles and all20stored parts; representative Pontax system supported without imposing its name on the separately named southern branch. No necessary geographic source gap remains.
records.supported_name_scope: The named northern river and its common lower receiving corridor, researched together with the selected southern Machisakahikanistikw branch. Does not rename every selected branch or wetland passage.

scope_limits: Individual unnamed feeder, wetland and pond names are not established. No true alias was supported.
Regional mapping is generalized and station081101 masks part of the upper route; independent imagery supplies ordinary corridor geography there, without adopting low-flow quantities.
Source and rendered sea terminals remain distinct; the separate tributary terminal is a confluence, not the marine outlet.
Exact banks, current wet channels, seasonal wetland hydraulics, tidal state, legal name extent and formal registry status remain unverified.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rivière Pontax
bounded_name_observations.scope: Named northern branch and supported common receiving system; representative name, not a uniform scalar name for every part.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rivière Machisakahikanistikw
bounded_name_observations.scope: Separately named southern branch selected within the mainstem fragment before its join with the Pontax; not a Pontax alias.

records.region: Oeiras do Pará and adjoining Cametá setting, Pará, Brazil
records.material_pending_reason: Two bounded connectors within one upper-feeder source-material-pending primary state: (1) the short chosen forested opening into the long wetland corridor; (2) the later eastward transfer across the vegetated Transcametá strip from that wetland to the mapped Anavera corridor. The wetland itself, named middle/lower receiving river, joins and actual ending are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No completed whole-selection representative is assigned. Rio Araticu remains a supported bounded receiving-system candidate; Rio Anavera belongs to the separately named middle reach.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research concludes with one material-pending primary state. Both mainstem fragments at stages 3 and 2, all 29 stored parts and the distinct source/render ending descriptions are accounted for; two upper receiving links remain unestablished.
records.supported_name_scope: No completed whole-selection representative is assigned. Rio Araticu remains a supported bounded receiving-system candidate; Rio Anavera belongs to the separately named middle reach.

scope_limits: No natural-river or lake name is established for the chosen opening and southern wetland.
The unresolved cross-connections are not supplied by overall basin proximity or by the pinned selected path itself; no claim that either connection is absent is made.
The maps are historical generalized compilations, and the imagery scene date is unestablished. Small features may be hidden by canopy, land use or scattered cloud.
Different printed Anavera/Anauerá spellings remain bounded observations without a formal equivalence or registry claim.
Coordinates and private point aids served orientation only. No geometry correction/revalidation, exact bank, instantaneous flow direction, tidal limit or hydraulic-operation conclusion is made.
The selected endpoint does not reach the full Araticu mouth in Rio Pará, despite the retained source sea class.

bounded_name_observations.scope: Exact FAPESPA prose spelling of an eastern Araticu tributary. Its likely relation to the map’s Anavera is contextual; no formal name-equivalence verification or whole-feature alias is asserted.

bounded_name_observations.scope: Separately named joining river south of the broad receiving course; not an alias of Araticu or the chosen opening.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio Oeiras
bounded_name_observations.scope: Separate western joining river downstream; not the selected initial feeder and not an Araticu alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Furo do Oeiras
bounded_name_observations.scope: Side channel beside Ilha Grande in the lower-river context; not the selected whole-route name.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio Pará
bounded_name_observations.scope: Farther downstream estuarine receiving water beyond the selected ending. Not appended to the selection or assigned as its name.

bounded_receiving_system_candidate.name: Rio Araticu
bounded_receiving_system_candidate.scope: Mapped middle/lower receiving river and actual terminal setting only. It is not a completed representative for the whole selected composite until the two upper connector limits are resolved.

records.region: Southern Baffin Island, Nunavut; southward lake-and-river corridor to the southern marine coast
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: No whole-selection natural-river name is supported. The inspected imagery supplies connected geographic context but no hydronym labels.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No whole-selection natural-river name is supported. The inspected imagery supplies connected geographic context but no hydronym labels.
records.completion_scope: Full bounded ordinary geographic correspondence is complete. Whole-selection naming is unsupported and retained as a completed null name-scope hold; no essential geographic source-material gap remains and no further source request is pending.
records.supported_name_scope: No whole-selection natural-river name is supported. The inspected imagery supplies connected geographic context but no hydronym labels.

scope_limits: No supported proper name or true alias for the whole natural-river selection, selected feeder, lakes or lower inlet has been established. This does not prove that official names do not exist.

The photographic mosaic includes clouds, shadows and a darker lower-valley tile; the visible receiving terrain supports ordinary corridor continuity, not fine-scale wet-channel or hydraulic conclusions.

The final rendered segment is a generalized marine extension and crosses part of an inlet-side land margin. It is kept distinct from the actual source sea endpoint and is not described as a literal river channel.
Names, exact bank positions, current discharge, tidal limit, lake levels and legal registry scope remain unverified.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
